names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 29 martie, «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Marcu, Episcopul Aretuselor».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 29 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Μάρκος επίσκοπος Αρεθουσίων …», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 29 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети Марко Исповедник, епископ Аретусијски у Сирији“, with the rank words Свети and Исповедник left off and with the see епископ Аретусијски у Сирији left off as well, this folder keeping the see in `office` and the place in its English name. The heading gives no epithet beyond the see, so the bare forename is what the source gives.

floruit.note: The life quotes St Gregory of Nazianzus's first oration against Julian: Mark pulled down the idol-temple «în împărăţia marelui Constantin», and the townsmen's revenge broke out «sub împăratul Iulian Apostatul (361-363)», the years doxologia.ro prints. He was an old man then, and the life ends with the Arethusians letting him go alive; no year is given for his death.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 29 martie — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Marcu, Episcopul Aretuselor»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 29ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Μάρκος επίσκοπος Αρεθουσίων, Κύριλλος διάκονος, και των εν Ασκάλωνι και Γάζη παρθένων γυναικών και ιερωμένων ανδρών»

attestations.note: The page gives him a conciliar career the Romanian life does not: the Council of Antioch in 341, where its Acts preserve an «Ἔκθεσις Πίστεως Μάρκου Ἀρεθουσίων»; the embassy of bishops to Trier in 342 to meet the emperor Constans; the Council of Philippopolis in 343; the Council of Sirmium in 351, which condemned Photinus of Sirmium as a follower of Marcellus of Ancyra; and the Council of Seleucia in Isauria in 358. It also ends the story differently from a martyrdom: after the tortures the idolaters repented, he became their teacher, and «Ο Άγιος Μάρκος κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη», he fell asleep in peace. This folder's `types` carry `hieromartyr` from the Romanian reading and are left as they are; the Greek reading is recorded here. The page's own gloss puts Arethusa «στα ανατολικά του Νομού Θεσσαλονίκης», in eastern Thessalonica, which does not agree with the Syrian Arethusa of the rest of its account, and nothing of that gloss is taken. It prints two apolytikia; the first, which names him and his companions, is added to this folder, and the second is the common of martyrs and is not.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 11.04.2026 (29. март ст. ст.) — „Свети Марко Исповедник, епископ Аретусијски у Сирији“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep in this folder, and the same story: the temple pulled down in the reign of Constantine, the reaction under Julian, the price set on the ruined temple, the honey and the stinging insects, and the townsmen won over in the end. It names both of the writers the other two calendars draw on, свети Григорије Богослов and блажени Теодорит. New to the folder: that some of the Arethusians themselves denied Christ when Julian apostatised and that it was they who rose against Mark; that his ears were cut off with a thin strong cord; that his face was bright as an angel of God though he was very old; and that the idolaters lowered the price of their temple step by step, almost to nothing, to keep him alive, and he would not give one coin. The entry gives no year at all — it dates by the two emperors' reigns only — so the floruit this folder already holds from doxologia.ro is untouched. The heading ranks him Исповедник, confessor, and that word was **not** taken into `types`: this folder carries `hieromartyr` from the Romanian reading, the Greek row's note already records that saint.gr has him fall asleep in peace, and the Prologue's own account likewise ends with him released alive and teaching; which rank is right is a disagreement between the sources and not a reader's to settle, so it is recorded here and nothing in `types` was changed. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. The stored form Марко folds with `mark-of-byblos` and `mark-of-ephesus`, which hold the same bare form; the fold is recorded as deliberate.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinţilor Sfinţiţi Mucenici Marcu, Episcopul Aretuselor, Chiril diaconul şi al celor împreună cu dânşii (the page prints «nesctricăciunii»)

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contending won from Thee, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Thy strength they overthrew the tormentors, and broke also the feeble insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.tone: Ἦχος δ’. Ὁ ὑψωθεῖς ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ.
hymns.text: Ἀρεθουσίων ὁ σοφὸς Ποιμενάρχης, ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ Μᾶρκε στερρῶς ἠνωνίσω, ἐν τὴ Φοινίκη δὲ ὢ Κύριλλε Διάκονε, Μάρτυς ὤφθης ἔνθεος, καὶ ἐν Γάζῃ τὴ πόλει, ἅμα καὶ Ἀσκάλωνι, Ἱερεῖς θεοφόροι, μετὰ Γυναίων ἤθλησον σεμνῶν, οὖς ὡς ὀπλίτας, Χριστοῦ μακαρίσωμεν.

source.text: saint.gr — Άγιος Μάρκος επίσκοπος Αρεθουσίων, Κύριλλος διάκονος, και των εν Ασκάλωνι και Γάζη, Ἀπολυτίκιον. It is one hymn for the whole company and names Mark, Cyril, the God-bearing priests and the modest women in turn. Recorded with kind troparion, which is the schema's word for it.

english.text: Mark, wise chief shepherd of Arethusa, you contended stoutly for Christ; and in Phoenicia you, O Cyril the deacon, were shown a martyr filled with God; and in the city of Gaza, and at Ascalon with it, God-bearing priests together with modest women contended — whom let us call blessed as the armed men of Christ.
